value.title: Leveraging Caches to Accelerate Hash Tables and Memoization

value.statement: Flat-HTA stores fixed-size key/value pairs associatively within the single cache line selected by hashing. Invalid sentinel keys hash to a different line; deleted keys differ from invalid keys, prevent lookup from terminating, and are reusable by update/swap.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.statement: Table descriptors specify starting address/size; four are supported in the described implementation. Lookup handles up to four key words and one value word. The x86-64 integer example uses64-bit registers. Found keys or available invalid slots resolve with a taken branch; absent keys in a full line fall through to software.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.statement: Update changes a matching key or reusable slot and otherwise falls through without modification. Full-line swap installs the new pair and returns a randomly selected victim key/value to software. Delete writes a deleted-key sentinel on a hit and falls through on a miss.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.statement: Software overflow stores displaced pairs. Full-swap insertion software preserves the victim and removes a stale copy of the newly inserted key if present. Software counters can trigger table resizing/reinsertion of all pairs.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.statement: An HTA functional unit hashes using x86 CRC32 with power-of-two table sizes, fetches one line, compares keys and resolves the branch/result. Decoder emits operand-feed, start, branch and result micro-operations; existing prediction mechanisms overlap the software or continuation path.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.statement: Atomic HTA instructions handle resolved operations. Software fallback uses line locks and lookup recheck after acquiring a lock; thread-safe insertion first tries no-eviction update and performs swap under the fallback lock. This does not certify an arbitrary Python or unlocked software map.
limitations: Paper-level Flat-HTA integer-word subset; exact ISA/compiler/hash/atomic implementation identity and consumer wrapper still require binding.

value.locator: PDFpp4-6 §3.2/§4.3 plus owned synthetic table_contract regression
value.statement: A consumer that skips all software bookkeeping on a taken branch can leave a stale overflow key after deleted-slot reuse and expose it after deletion. The tested single-threaded wrapper enforces exclusive ownership on every insertion/deletion. This is a source-derived integration obligation, not a demonstrated fault in an authenticated published wrapper.
limitations: New synthetic instruction/consumer sequence only; actual published software wrappers and concurrent behavior not inspected or certified.

value.description: Hash-key cache-line map with explicit resolved/fallback branch interface and software overflow; no general indexed-memory or atomic-RMW capability inheritance.

value.summary: One hashed cache-line key map with resolved/fallback branch instructions and software victim handling; conservative integer-word subset.

interface.software_supplies: Table descriptor/base/size, integer key tuple and optional value, reserved-slot sentinel/hash setup, continuation target and software overflow/ownership strategy.
interface.invocation: hta_lookup/update/swap/delete; resolved operations branch to continuation, unresolved operations execute the software path. Concurrent fallback locks and rechecks.
interface.outputs: Lookup hit/miss or fallback status, optional matching value, and displaced victim pair on full-line swap.

realization.description: Return a matching key value or resolved miss; absent key with no invalid slot requires software overflow lookup. Complete the original software fallback and ownership protocol; concurrent maps require atomic instructions, lock/recheck and locked eviction.

result.form: Return a matching key value or resolved miss; absent key with no invalid slot requires software overflow lookup.
result.validity: Explicit Flat-HTA key map, correct hash/line/sentinel/descriptor and complete software consumer. A returned eviction victim is not the old value of the requested key.

ordering.scope: One key operation plus its necessary software fallback
ordering.description: Branch taken means hardware resolution, not necessarily key found or no software ownership obligation. Atomic fast path and locked concurrent fallback must be established separately.

requirements.description: Bind exact table/word count, descriptor, power-of-two geometry, actual CRC/hash and each selected line. No missing-line/context default is allowed.
Sentinel values must hash away from the line they mark. Lookup must not treat deleted as invalid; update/swap may reuse it.
Bind hardware/software duplicate cleanup on insertion and deletion, victim preservation and resizing. The paper full-swap cleanup alone does not establish an arbitrary mixed-operation wrapper.
Prove atomic hardware operations and software fallback lock/recheck, update-before-lock and swap-under-lock protocol before concurrent use.
Differentiate resolved miss from hit and unresolved fallback; do not expose undefined miss value as0 or return an eviction victim as the requested key old value.
Authenticate actual ISA/register packing/compiler/hash/atomic/software wrapper and memory translation/coherence/protection. Do not import physical stash restrictions from Hierarchical-HTA.

parameters.notes: Fig4 cache-line reference; raw helper capacity derives from fixed key/value words.
Architectural descriptor reference, not table owner/context count.

internal_mechanisms.description: One hash-selected cache line holds any matching key in its fixed pair slots; separate software map stores overflow.
Functional unit receives key words/table descriptor, hashes and fetches one line, compares keys, resolves branch and result.
Unresolved paths preserve victims and handle stale key copies; concurrent paths lock and recheck before fallback access.
Existing branch prediction overlaps software or continuation execution; actual misprediction/retirement obligations require implementation binding.
Instruction resolves branch/result; unresolved logical map operation still requires software completion and concurrency protocol.

limitations: Raw-word helper models a finite single-threaded normalized table, not ISA execution, actual CRC32 or atomic/cache behavior.
Its mixed-operation cleanup is an explicit corrected consumer contract, not proof of published wrapper source.
No floating-point equality/type, general gather/CAS or Hierarchical-HTA stash capabilities.
Actual implementation/register packing and concurrency behavior remain unbound.
